title: Interweaving participation formats to strengthen representation and deliberation in urban mobility transformations. Lessons from designing Kiezblocks in Berlin
journal: GAIA - Ecological Perspectives for Science and Society
abstract: How can cities engage diverse residents in urban mobility transformations? Drawing on a multi-format participation process for two Berlin Kiezblocks, this paper shows that combining participation formats with different recruitment methods, interaction types, and levels of public influence on planning decisions can strengthen representation and constructive deliberation.Engaging residents in urban mobility transformations can support implementation by mitigating polarization and strengthening governance, yet designing inclusive participation processes remains challenging. We present a multi-format participation process for two Kiezblocks in Berlin-Mitte, developed with municipal planners, to engage diverse residents in constructive deliberation (external inclusion), make their perspectives heard (internal inclusion), and enable different levels of public influence on planning decisions. Drawing on field notes and structured reflections within the transdisciplinary consortium, we describe the participation formats including their recruitment methods, interaction types, and main strengths and weaknesses. Although suitable format combinations depend on goals, target groups, and local contexts, experiences suggest that interweaving stakeholder meetings, targeted outreach formats, and formats based on random selection can strengthen inclusion while providing different levels of public influence on planning decisions. Targeted outreach formats were particularly valuable for engaging groups underrepresented in participation processes, including children and residents with migration background, while formats with random selection helped counter misleading perceptions of polarization. In contrast, formats based on self-selection, including online participation and town hall meetings, appeared more susceptible to domination by louder voices and less conducive to constructive deliberation, with implications for designing participation processes for sustainability transformations.

title: Yahoo Plus and the Domestication of Money-Ritual: A Cultural Analysis of Cyber Fraud and Spirituality in Nigeria
abstract: The phenomenon known as Yahoo Plus represents a contemporary Nigerian development in which cyber fraud becomes connected with ritual practices believed to enhance financial success. Yahoo refers to internet fraud carried out mostly by young people who deceive foreign victims through various online schemes. Over time, the practice developed into Yahoo Plus, where practitioners combine digital fraud with ritual or spiritual activities believed to increase their chances of obtaining money from victims. This paper examines Yahoo Plus as a Nigerian adaptation of the wider human belief in ritual wealth. Across many cultures, wealth has often been associated with supernatural contracts, sacrifice or mystical intervention. In Nigeria, this idea has been domesticated within the context of cybercrime. The study explains the concept of Yahoo, its operation as internet fraud and the socio-economic factors that encourage young people to participate in it, including unemployment, social pressure and the influence of social media. It also examines how Yahoo gradually evolved into Yahoo Plus when fraudsters believed they needed supernatural assistance to continue deceiving victims who had become more aware of online scams. The study relies on qualitative data gathered from online sources, scholarly literature, news reports and observations from social media discussions that reflect public perceptions of Yahoo and Yahoo Plus. Through this approach, the paper explains the emergence of Yahoo, the transformation of internet fraud into Yahoo Plus, and the socio-economic factors that encourage young people to participate in the practice. The study argues that Yahoo Plus reflects a deeper cultural process in which traditional beliefs about ritual wealth are adapted to modern digital practices.

title: Values or competencies? Explaining collective social entrepreneurial intention among young people: a mixed-methods approach
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how young people develop the intention to create a social economy enterprise and addresses a key question: Do traditional models of entrepreneurial intention adequately explain collective and socially oriented forms of entrepreneurship? Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a sample of 2,000 young individuals (18–34) in Quebec, including 733 with entrepreneurial intentions, this study combines regression analysis and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to capture both net effects and configurational pathways. Findings The results challenge and qualify dominant intention models. Core predictors of the theory of planned behavior (TPB), such as entrepreneurial self-efficacy and attitude, are not significant in this context. Instead, intention is primarily shaped by subjective norms and value orientations, with altruistic values and low egoistic orientations emerging as central drivers. The configurational analysis reveals multiple pathways to intention, highlighting the role of socially embedded and value-driven mechanisms. Research limitations/implications The study relies on single-item measures and a context-specific indicator of social economy knowledge, which calls for cautious interpretation. Future research should develop validated multi-item scales and examine additional individual, relational and institutional factors, including identity and ecosystem influences. Practical implications The findings suggest that fostering collective social entrepreneurship among young people requires moving beyond traditional skill-based approaches. Educational and support programs should emphasize value development, collective engagement and awareness of the social economy, while addressing persistent misconceptions. Originality/value By integrating the value-attitude-behavior model with the TPB, this study demonstrates that individual-centric models have limited explanatory power in collective social entrepreneurship contexts. It reframes entrepreneurial intention as a socially embedded and value-driven process, extending the boundaries of intention-based models in entrepreneurship research.

title: Using stories to promote information literacy
abstract: Purpose Over many years, experts have devised various models for teaching and learning information literacy skills. The underpinnings of most are unclear, however, and they can seem very abstract to students. The project discussed counters these problems by presenting a framework of information literacy principles derived from a fiction story familiar to the targeted children. Design/methodology/approach During the course of one academic year, the model was deployed in two separate independent learning projects undertaken by the same class. The paper outlines the resulting benefits and caveats that should be considered. Findings The children enjoyed working with the model, particularly as it encouraged them to emulate the heroine of the story on which the framework was based. It also gave context to the employment of information skills. The model did not, however, address every scenario that emerged in the children's work. Research limitations/implications Although the framework was twice applied in-context with students, only one class in one year group and at one school was involved. Practical implications The success of the project, albeit on a small scale, attests to the probability that practitioners elsewhere will be able to repeat the work with good results or devise similarly effective models. Originality/value The paper deals with an area rarely covered in information literacy studies. It is highly unusual for a teaching and learning framework to be derived from a work of fiction in the way proposed here.

title: Unlike most biomarkers, Lp(a) is far less forgiving on selectivity and metrological shortcomings
abstract: Abstract Despite being an established causal risk factor for ASCVD, lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) remains one of the most misunderstood metrics in cardiovascular risk assessment and clinical practice. Standardization of Lp(a) measurement remains challenging due to the marked heterogeneity in apolipoprotein(a) isoform size and co-existence of genetic variants, which affect immunoassay calibration and inter-method comparability, potentially leading to misclassification of cardiovascular risk and impacting clinical decision-making. Stakeholders concerned about accuracy of Lp(a) testing have spent decades trying to solve what was considered a calibration problem for Lp(a). We currently know there is also a measurand heterogeneity problem as revealed by Lp(a) assays with different selectivity’s. Consequently, Lp(a) harmonization ultimately requires a clearly defined measurand and supports the transition from mass-based to molar standardization.

title: Unified heuristic optimization (UHO) for scheduling repetitive and nonrepetitive construction and renewal projects
journal: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
abstract: Purpose Traditional Critical Path Method (CPM) based heuristics are insufficient for managing resource overallocation and meeting deadlines in repetitive projects such as highways and multi-bridge repairs. Despite their inefficiencies, they are still being used due to the lack of simple heuristic scheduling tools that help project managers and stakeholders cater to these projects' needs, such as crew continuity. The study aims to fill this gap and develop a unified framework that extends CPM heuristics to optimize scheduling for both repetitive and nonrepetitive projects. Design/methodology/approach A unified heuristic optimization (UHO) framework was developed, integrating CPM-based cost-resource allocation and time-cost trade-off procedures with the first-come-first-served repetitive scheduling methodology. An Excel-based automated scheduling tool based on the proposed framework was developed as a proof of concept and tested against cases from the literature. Findings This article presented a novel scheduling framework that generalizes CPM procedures to be applicable for repetitive projects, resolving any deadline or resource allocation constraints. Applied to a literature case study, the produced schedule achieved the same overall project deadline while having more efficient resource utilization. Originality/value This study introduces a unified heuristic approach that simplifies and enhances scheduling for repetitive infrastructure projects. By bridging the gap between CPM-based tools and the unique demands of repetitive scheduling, it supports project managers in managing the schedule and resources of large-scale repetitive projects.

title: Transforming teaching practices: the role of technology-enhanced pedagogy in advancing higher education learning
abstract: Purpose Technology-enhanced pedagogy (TEP) is increasingly recognised as being associated with innovation in higher education. It offers opportunities to facilitate more interactive, inclusive and engaging learning environments. This study investigates how lecturers in universities adopt TEP and examines its associations with student engagement. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative survey-based design. The research was grounded in the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework. Data were collected via a structured 46-item questionnaire using Google Forms. The participants included both lecturers and students. The dataset was analysed using SPSS and AMOS to assess direct, indirect and moderating relationships. Findings The results indicate that TEP is significantly associated with higher levels of student engagement. This relationship is facilitated by inclusive and participatory teaching practices. However, variations in educators’ digital competency are linked to inconsistent implementation. This suggests a need for ongoing professional development initiatives. Furthermore, the findings show that sustainable leadership and organisational development are related to the impact of TEP on engagement. Practical implications The study highlights the importance of TPACK-oriented training. Such training should integrate tool mastery with discipline-specific applications, assessment redesign and classroom implementation. The study recommends knowledge-sharing structures, such as communities of practice and teaching academies, to scale successful innovations. Crucially, the findings suggest that individual lecturer competence is most effective when supported by institutional routines and leadership alignment. Therefore, professional development should be embedded within a broader culture of organisational learning. Originality/value This study integrates TEP with TPACK and various organisational dimensions. It contributes novel insights into how technology-driven pedagogy is associated with higher levels of student engagement and institutional learning.

title: The terroir paradox: institutional barriers to rural–urban food integration in western Türkiye
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Ödemiş's rural food production connects with İzmir's urban gastronomy market in western Türkiye, primarily from the perspective of rural and locally embedded food-system actors. It focuses on supply-side, institutional, and relational barriers shaping market access and the conversion of production capacity into urban market representation. Design/methodology/approach An interpretivist qualitative case study was conducted with 17 purposively selected stakeholders relevant to the Ödemiş–İzmir food system. Interview data were contextualised with official agricultural statistics and geographical indication (GI)-related documentary sources and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke (2006, 2019). Findings were interpreted through terroir, social capital and collective action theories. Findings Six themes and 24 sub-themes were identified. Despite strong gastronomic capacity, including GI-registered potatoes and olive oil and a strong dairy sector, Ödemiş remains underrepresented in İzmir. Key barriers include rising input costs, logistics deficits and negative assessments of cooperative effectiveness. Integration relies largely on informal personal networks rather than institutionalised channels and is further constrained by weak promotion and intergenerational knowledge erosion. Originality/value The study proposes the “terroir paradox” – the disconnect between strong production terroir and weak distribution and representation terroir – as a framework for examining interruptions in the transmission of territorial value to urban markets. The findings suggest that institutional capacity and bridging relationships matter alongside product quality. The framework extends production-centric understandings of terroir and offers propositions for comparative testing.

title: Structural empowerment and psychosocial safety climate in healthcare: a systematic integrative review
journal: Journal of Health Organization and Management
abstract: Purpose Psychosocial safety climate (PSC) is associated with nurses' well-being, yet the organisational conditions under which shared PSC perceptions form remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on structural empowerment (SE) theory, PSC theory, and organisational sensemaking, this review derives propositions on the SE–PSC association in healthcare organisations. Design/methodology/approach A systematic integrative review (PRISMA 2020) of five databases identified 30 studies. The synthesis combined deductive framework analysis with abductive theorising; methodological quality was appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings Three propositions emerged. In the resulting framework, leadership and governance are conceptualised as organisational cues in collective sensemaking, resource availability as a signal of management commitment, and role clarity and development opportunities as signals of organisational values. Formal arrangements did not consistently correspond to nurses' experienced authority or access. These patterns support an interpretive account in which leadership coherence, resource provision, and accessible development opportunities may be associated with shared PSC perceptions. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional designs preclude causal inference. Empirical support was stronger for Propositions 1 and 2 than for Proposition 3. Validated PSC instruments remain underused; the propositions require longitudinal and multilevel validation. Practical implications Nursing management should align leadership practices, resource allocation, and role clarity as credible signals of organisational commitment to psychological health. Social implications The framework offers an evidence-informed basis for policies improving nurses' psychosocial work environments and workforce retention. Originality/value The review reconceptualises SE as an interpretive context for PSC formation, offering grounded propositions for empirical testing.
